subject: CHEM
title: General Chemistry for Engineering Students
description: Introduction to important concepts and principles of chemistry; emphasis on areas considered most relevant in an engineering context; practical applications of chemical principles in engineering and technology. Students completing CHEM 107 and changing majors to curricula requiring CHEM 101 and CHEM 102 may substitute CHEM 107 for CHEM 101. Only one of the following will satisfy the requirements for a degree: CHEM 107 or CHEM 101.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Concurrent enrollment in CHEM 117; grade of C or better in MATH 150, or equivalent, or acceptable score on Texas A&M University math placement exam; also taught at Galveston and Qatar campuses.

subject: CHEM
title: General Chemistry for Engineering Students Laboratory
description: Introduction to important concepts and principles of chemistry in the laboratory; emphasis on areas considered most relevant in an engineering context; practical applications of chemical principles in engineering and technology. Students completing CHEM 117 and changing majors to curricula requiring CHEM 111 and CHEM 112 may substitute CHEM 117 for CHEM 111. Only one of the following will satisfy the requirements for a degree: CHEM 117 or CHEM 111.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: CHEM 107 or registration therein; also taught at Galveston and Qatar campuses.

subject: ENGL
title: ENGL 103 or ENGL 104 (Introduction to Rhetoric and Composition)
description: A first-year writing course on academic reading, argument, research, and revision. Students write for different audiences and purposes.
notes: Student chooses one: Introduction to Rhetoric and Composition | Composition and Rhetoric.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)

subject: ENGR
title: Engineering Lab I - Computation
description: Introduction to the design and development of computer applications for engineers; computation to enhance problem solving abilities; basic concepts of software design through the implementation and debugging of student-written programs; introduction to engineering majors, career exploration, engineering practice within realistic constraints, e.g. economic, environmental, ethical, health and safety, and sustainability; pathways to success in engineering.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MATH 151 or MATH 150, or concurrent enrollment; admission to the college of engineering.

subject: MATH
title: Engineering Mathematics I
description: Rectangular coordinates, vectors, analytic geometry, functions, limits, derivatives of functions, applications, integration, computer algebra. MATH 171 designed to be a more demanding version of this course. Only one of the following will satisfy the requirements for a degree: MATH 131, MATH 142, MATH 147, MATH 151 or MATH 171.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MATH 150 or equivalent or acceptable score on TAMU Math Placement Exam; also taught at Galveston and Qatar campuses.

subject: ENGR
title: Experimental Physics and Engineering Lab II - Mechanics
description: Description and application of laws of physical motion to the solution of science and engineering problems; using sensing, control and actuation for experimental verification of physics concepts while solving engineering problems.
notes: Cross-listed as PHYS 216.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MATH 151 or MATH 171 or equivalent; grade of C or better in ENGR 102; grade of C or better in PHYS 206 or concurrent enrollment; also taught at Galveston campus.

subject: MATH
title: Engineering Mathematics II
description: Differentiation and integration techniques and their applications (area, volumes, work), improper integrals, approximate integration, analytic geometry, vectors, infinite series, power series, Taylor series, computer algebra. MATH 172 designed to be a more demanding version of this course. Only one of the following will satisfy the requirements for a degree: MATH 148, MATH 152 or MATH 172.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MATH 151 or equivalent; grade of C or better in MATH 150 or equivalent, or acceptable score on TAMU Math Placement Exam; also taught at Galveston campus.

subject: PHYS
title: Newtonian Mechanics for Engineering and Science
description: Calculus-based introductory Newtonian mechanics; laws of physical motion for solution of science and engineering problems.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MATH 151 or MATH 171, or equivalent; also taught at Galveston and Qatar campuses.

subject: CSCE
title: Introduction to Computing
description: Introduction to the broad field of computing; presentations from industry and academia about how computer science concepts are used in research and end products; includes a major writing component.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)

subject: CSCE
title: Program Design and Concepts
description: Extension of prior programming knowledge and creation of computer programs that solve problems; application of computational thinking to enhance problem solving; analysis of, design of and implementation of computer programs; use of basic and aggregate data types; encapsulation and abstraction; development of software that uses dynamic memory and avoids memory leaks; study of error handling strategies to develop more secure and robust programs.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in ENGR 102, CSCE 110, CSCE 111, CSCE 206 or PHYS 150.

subject: CSCE
title: Discrete Structures for Computing
description: Mathematical foundations from discrete mathematics for analyzing computer algorithms, for both correctness and performance; introduction to models of computation, including finite state machines and Turing machines.
notes: Cross-listed as ECEN 222.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MATH 142, MATH 147, MATH 151, or MATH 171.

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra
description: Introductory course in linear algebra covering abstract ideas of vector space and linear transformation as well as models and applications of these concepts, such as systems of linear equations, matrices and determinants; MATH 323 designed to be a more demanding version of this course. Only one of the following will satisfy the requirements for a degree: MATH 304, MATH 307, MATH 309, MATH 311, or MATH 323.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)

subject: CSCE
title: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Specification and implementation of basic abstract data types and their associated algorithms including stacks, queues, lists, sorting and selection, searching, graphs and hashing; performance tradeoffs of different implementations and asymptotic analysis of running time and memory usage.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade C or better in CSCE 120 or CSCE 121; grade of C or better in CSCE 222 or ECEN 222, or concurrent enrollment.

subject: CSCE
title: Computer Organization
description: Computer systems from programmer's perspective including simple logic design, data representation and processor architecture, programming of processors, memory, control flow, input/output, and performance measurements; hands-on lab assignments.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CSCE 221, or concurrent enrollment.

subject: CSCE
title: Programming Languages
description: Exploration of the design space of programming languages via an in-depth study of functional and object-oriented programming concepts, using concrete programming languages as examples. Focuses on idiomatic uses of programming language constructs and on features characteristic for each language.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CSCE 221, or concurrent enrollment.

title: COMM 203 or COMM 205 or ENGL 210 (Public Speaking)

notes: Student chooses one: Public Speaking | Communication for Technical Professions | Technical and Professional Writing.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)

plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)

subject: CSCE
title: Computing Ethics
description: Introduction to legal, social and ethical issues in computing and software development; emphasizes ethical decision-making, professional responsibility and communication, with coverage of professional codes, organizational ethics, law and policy, intellectual property, open-source software and variety of contemporary topics.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CSCE 221; also taught at Galveston campus.

subject: CSCE
title: Introduction to Computer Systems
description: Introduction to system support for application programs, both on single node and over network including OS application interface, inter-process communication, introduction to system and network programming, and simple computer security concepts; hands-on lab assignments.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: CSCE 221 with a grade of C or better; grade of C or better in CSCE 312 or concurrent enrollment in CSCE 350/ECEN 350 or ECEN 350/CSCE 350.

subject: CSCE
title: Foundations of Software Engineering
description: Intensive programming experience and provision of the fundamentals needed for larger-scale software development; integration of concepts in computer science and familiarization with a variety of programming and development tools and techniques; team projects each with an emphasis on a different specialization within computer science; emphasis on programming techniques to ease code integration and clarity; practical exposure to software-engineering processes through large-scale projects and specification and documentation.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CSCE 314, CSCE 350/ECEN 350, or ECEN 350/CSCE 350; grade of C or better or concurrent enrollment in CSCE 313.

subject: STAT
title: Principles of Statistics I
description: Introduction to probability and probability distributions; sampling and descriptive measures; inference and hypothesis testing; linear regression, analysis of variance.

subject: CSCE
title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
description: Study of computer algorithms for numeric and non-numeric problems; design paradigms; analysis of time and space requirements of algorithms; correctness of algorithms; NP-completeness and undecidability of problems.
plan: Plan of Study, 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (first year common to Engineering, then CS years 2-4)
